Neha / Sarah — quick technical summary (scope: server snapshots + activity logs).

What happens today: backups and offsite snapshots follow our 90-day standard TTL for production volumes. Automatic purge jobs run weekly; snapshots marked with a legal hold flag are excluded from the purge pipeline.

What we can offer for this audit:
- Legal hold window: default 30 days, extendable to 90 days with internal approval (ops + privacy). If you need an interim option, we can do 45 days without an SLA change.
- Export format: we produce encrypted tar.gz archives (AES-256), accompanied by SHA256 checksums and an export manifest that lists object keys and record counts.
- Export timeline: once scope and hold are confirmed, expect 5–8 business days for snapshot extraction and archive assembly (longer if redaction is required).
- Subprocessors that may see data during export:
  * LogSight (log ingestion/processing vendor) — may see metadata during retrieval jobs.
  * CloudStorage partner (object storage backing snapshots) — handles encrypted objects only; no plaintext processing.
  * TransferOps (managed transfer service) — participates only if outbound transfer uses their courier workflow.

Security notes: all transfers use encrypted channels (TLS 1.3 + server-side AES-256 at rest), keys are customer-rotated on request, and access is limited to named ops personnel for the export window.

Operational constraint: if a scheduled retention purge job falls inside the requested hold start and we do not receive a signed hold request beforehand, the snapshot may be evicted per schedule. To guarantee preservation, we need an approved hold request in our system 72 hours before any scheduled purge run.

-Karthik
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
